Project Details..

Project Title: Abandoned but Not Forgotten: The Stories Behind NASA's Space Equipment

What does the project do?

Our project explores NASA's equipment left behind during space exploration missions on the Moon, Mars and in deep space. It presents the history, purpose and scientific contributions of these objects through educational storytelling. We focus on missions such as Apollo, Curiosity, InSight, Perseverance, Voyager, Pioneer and New Horizons.

How does it work?

The project organizes space equipment and missions into three main categories:

  • Moon: Apollo lunar experiments, seismometers and laser retroreflectors.
  • Mars: Curiosity, InSight and Perseverance, highlighting their discoveries about the Red Planet.
  • Deep Space: Voyager, Pioneer and New Horizons, exploring humanity's journey beyond the outer planets.

Each story explains what the equipment was designed to do, what discoveries it helped achieve and why its scientific contribution remains valuable.

Benefits and intended impact

The project makes space science easier and more interesting for school students and young space enthusiasts. It encourages curiosity, improves awareness of NASA missions and promotes STEM education. It also communicates an important message: equipment left behind is not necessarily useless or forgotten; it can continue to contribute to scientific knowledge long after its original mission.

Tools and technologies used

Our current project deliverables were prepared using:

  • NASA mission information and educational resources for research.
  • Microsoft PowerPoint for the project demonstration.
  • Digital documentation and content-writing tools for organizing the stories and explanations.

This submission is an educational storytelling concept. It does not claim to include a completed software application, physical prototype or custom hardware.

Creativity and innovation

The creative aspect of our project is presenting abandoned space equipment from a different perspective. Instead of focusing only on spacecraft and successful missions, we highlight the instruments and equipment that remain behind and the discoveries they made possible. By connecting scientific facts with storytelling, we aim to make space exploration more relatable, memorable and inspiring.

Factors considered

Our team considered scientific accuracy, educational value, simplicity of language, accessibility for younger audiences and the importance of highlighting the long-term contributions of NASA missions.
